description: The Catalan Surveillance Network of SARS-CoV-2 in Sewage began in July 2020 to monitor 56 wastewater treatment plants across Catalonia whose sewage represents about 80% of the population. A 24-hour flow-proportional composite of raw sewage is taken weekly at each plant inlet and sent within 24 hours to reference laboratories, which concentrate the sample, extract RNA and quantify two target genes (N1/N2 or N1/IP4). The released tables give, for each plant and sampling date, gene copies per litre for each target, the plant's daily inflow, rain events and comments. The network is funded by the Catalan Government and coordinated by the Catalan Water Agency, the Catalan Public Health Agency and the Catalan Institute for Water Research; data are released periodically on Zenodo from a GitHub repository, and a dashboard exists. Caveats: the version read (1.3, October 2020) is a small file with a newer version available, no licence is stated on the record page, and the dashboard did not render in a headless browser. Simulation uses: a plant-level wastewater signal with inflow and rainfall for epidemic early warning. Related records: Germany's AMELAG (data-rki-amelag-wastewater-surveillance) and the US NWSS (data-cdc-nwss-wastewater-surveillance).
